_comment: PER-MARKET DOSSIERS for the international growth cluster.
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-15-international-growth-cluster-design.md
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
Shingle-overlap catches duplication only AFTER a page is written. This file
catches thinness BEFORE. A page may not be written until its dossier is filled,
and verify-cluster-pages.js fails the page if the market-specific facts listed
here are not actually present in the rendered HTML.
RULES
1. requiredMentions must contain at least 8 entries, each a market-SPECIFIC
string: a named statute, regulation, curriculum document, exam board,
institution, dataset, operator or place. Generic marketing words do not
count and defeat the purpose.
2. No string in requiredMentions may appear in another market's dossier.
That is the anti-duplication rule, enforced by the gate.
3. localProject must name a real dataset from that market with a real
analytical trap. This is the strongest anti-duplication device we have.
4. sources must contain at least 3 primary sources, with the claim each one
supports. If a claim cannot be sourced, it does not go on the page.
A claim that resists sourcing gets stated as unconfirmed, or dropped.
The New Jersey entry records a real lesson: the widely repeated claim that AP
computer science satisfies part of a New Jersey mathematics credit could not be
confirmed at primary source, and second-hand accounts contradicted each other on
both the start year and which credit it covered. It was removed from the page.

coding-classes-in-georgia.curriculumAuthority: Georgia Code 20-2-149.3, Requirements for computer science education (SB 108, 2019). All middle schools in a local system must offer instruction in exploratory computer science, including state charter schools serving middle grades. High schools were phased: at least 50 percent of a system's high schools from 2023-24, all from 2024-25. The statute supplies an unusually BROAD definition of computer science, which is the page's second point: two schools can both comply while teaching very different things.
coding-classes-in-georgia.localProject: Base rates and conditional probability, anchored on published CDC prevalence figures, with Atlanta as the home of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Trap: given a positive result from a highly accurate screening test for a rare condition, most positives are FALSE positives, because the small error rate applies to the very large healthy population. Taught as a two by two table of counts for 100,000 people rather than as Bayes' theorem in symbols. Ninth distinct KIND of error. Deliberately distinguished from the Illinois class-imbalance project: Illinois is about choosing the right METRIC for an imbalanced problem, Georgia is about what a positive result actually MEANS once the base rate is known.
requiredMentions: algorithmic processes, coding, and logical thinking

sources.claim: Georgia Code 20-2-149.3 requires each local school system to provide that all middle schools offer instruction in exploratory computer science, and that state charter schools serving middle school students do the same. For high schools the duty is phased: beginning in the 2023-2024 school year at least 50 percent of a system's high schools must offer a course in computer science, and beginning in the 2024-2025 school year all of them must. The statute defines computer science as the study of computers, algorithmic processes, coding, and logical thinking, including computer principles, their hardware and software designs, their implementation, and their impact on society.
sources.citation: Official Code of Georgia Annotated 20-2-149.3, Requirements for computer science education

sources.claim: A student meeting the requirements to be a HOPE Scholar at the time of high school graduation must earn a minimum of four full rigor credits from the Academic Rigor Course List prior to graduating. Computer Science Principles and Games, Apps and Society are among the courses that satisfy HOPE rigor, and Advanced Placement courses in core subjects are approved rigor courses. The list is maintained by the Georgia Student Finance Commission.
sources.citation: Georgia Student Finance Commission, HOPE Scholarship initial academic eligibility and Academic Rigor Course List

sources.claim: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, and publishes prevalence figures for conditions that students can look up directly.
sources.citation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

rejectedClaims.claim: Georgia's computer science requirement came from HB 897.
rejectedClaims.why: Wrong bill, caught before writing. The requirement traces to SB 108 (2019), codified at O.C.G.A. 20-2-149.3. The initial research assumption was checked against the code section rather than trusted.

rejectedClaims.claim: A specific named test with specific sensitivity and specificity figures.
rejectedClaims.why: The page deliberately describes the screening test in general terms ('correctly identifies almost everybody who has the condition, wrongly flags only a small percentage of those who do not') and has students look up current CDC prevalence themselves, rather than printing invented or unsourced diagnostic accuracy numbers that would date badly and could be read as medical guidance.

coding-classes-in-washington.curriculumAuthority: Washington state computer science learning standards, referenced by RCW 28A.230.300 as the alignment test a course must meet before it can substitute for a third year mathematics or science course.
coding-classes-in-washington.localProject: Seattle Open Data, Fremont Bridge Bicycle Counter, running since October 2012 with hourly counts from inductive loops in the east and west pathways. Two traps, both about CONSTRUCT VALIDITY rather than statistics: (1) one bridge is not a city, so any claim about Seattle cycling drawn from a single sensor is a claim about that sensor; (2) the columns are east PATHWAY and west PATHWAY, not eastbound and westbound, and the loops count bicycles regardless of travel direction, so a commute-direction chart built from them measures which side of the bridge people ride on. Eighth distinct KIND of error: the variable does not mean what its name implies, and nothing was miscalculated. NOTE: no claim about counter outages or missing data appears on the page, because that could not be verified.
requiredMentions: third year mathematics or third year science

sources.claim: RCW 28A.230.300 permits a student to substitute a computer science course aligned to state computer science learning standards as an alternative to a third year mathematics or third year science course. Before approving it, the school counselor provides the student and the student's parent or guardian with written notification of the consequences of the substitution on postsecondary opportunities. The student, parent or guardian, and school counselor or principal must all agree; the substitution must align with the student's High School and Beyond Plan; and each student is limited to one such substitution.
sources.citation: Revised Code of Washington 28A.230.300, Computer science

sources.claim: RCW 28A.230.097 requires boards of directors to approve AP computer science courses as equivalent to high school mathematics or science, and to denote on a student's transcript that AP computer science qualifies as a math-based quantitative course for students who take the course in their senior year.
sources.citation: Revised Code of Washington 28A.230.097

sources.claim: The Fremont Bridge Bicycle Counter began operation in October 2012 and records bicycles crossing the bridge on the pedestrian and bicycle pathways. Inductive loops on the east and west pathways count the passing of bicycles REGARDLESS of travel direction. The data consists of a date and time field plus east and west pathway count fields giving the total bicycles detected in each one-hour period, published on the City of Seattle Open Data portal.
sources.citation: City of Seattle Open Data portal, Fremont Bridge Bicycle Counter

rejectedClaims.claim: The Fremont Bridge counter has documented outages that read as zeros, so missing data looks like a collapse in cycling.
rejectedClaims.why: Plausible and pedagogically attractive, but the dataset documentation reviewed did not confirm any specific outage or gap history, so it is not asserted on the page. The two traps that ARE taught (single-sensor sampling, and pathway columns not being directions) are both stated in the city's own dataset description.

rejectedClaims.claim: A specific Indian American population figure for Washington State.
rejectedClaims.why: Not verified at a source we were willing to cite, so no number appears on the page. The page names the tech-corridor cities instead, which is what the audience recognises anyway.

coding-classes-in-virginia.curriculumAuthority: 2017 Computer Science Standards of Learning, adopted November 2017, taught from 2019-20. Virginia was the FIRST state to require computer science instruction at all K-12 levels. K-8 is addressed WITHIN existing content areas; middle and high school are stand-alone electives. The page's spine is that integration is the most fragile delivery model: no timetable slot, no specialist teacher, no assessment to reveal absence.
coding-classes-in-virginia.localProject: Virginia School Quality Profiles / VDOE SOL pass rates, published for schools, divisions and the state across three years. Trap: REGRESSION TO THE MEAN. Select the bottom tenth of schools in year one and they rise in year two with no intervention, because selecting on an extreme selects partly for bad luck and luck does not repeat. Mirror it with the top tenth falling. Consequence: any programme aimed at the worst performers appears to work even if it does nothing, so an evaluation without a comparison group is worthless. Seventh distinct KIND of error in the cluster. Framed explicitly as being about statistics, not about judging schools.
requiredMentions: critical thinking, creative thinking, collaboration, communication, and citizenship

sources.claim: In November 2017 Virginia became the first state to require computer science instruction integrated at all K-12 levels, adopting K-12 Computer Science Standards of Learning, expected to be taught from the 2019-2020 academic year. Computer science in grades K-8 is addressed within the content areas, including language arts and history, while middle and high school classes are designed as stand-alone electives.
sources.citation: Virginia Department of Education, 2017 Computer Science Standards of Learning

sources.claim: A Standard Diploma requires at least 22 standard credits and 5 verified credits. An Advanced Studies Diploma requires at least 26 standard credits and 5 verified credits. Standard credits are earned by completing required and elective courses; verified credits are earned by completing required courses AND passing associated end-of-course SOL tests or other Board-approved assessments.
sources.citation: Virginia Department of Education, Standard and Advanced Studies Diploma graduation requirements

sources.claim: In accordance with the Profile of a Virginia Graduate, students shall acquire and demonstrate foundational skills in Virginia's 5 C's: critical thinking, creative thinking, collaboration, communication, and citizenship.
sources.citation: Virginia Department of Education, Profile of a Virginia Graduate

sources.claim: The Virginia Department of Education publishes School Quality Profiles containing accreditation, historical Standards of Learning scores and passing rates, and provides downloadable SOL test results for schools, school divisions and the state by grade level, course and content area covering three years with numerators and denominators.
sources.citation: Virginia Department of Education, SOL Test Pass Rates and Other Results; Virginia School Quality Profiles

sources.claim: Virginia has 157,635 Indian Americans, 1.83 percent of the state population.
sources.citation: 2020 United States Census

rejectedClaims.claim: Because Virginia requires computer science K-12, every Virginia child is learning to code.
rejectedClaims.why: The requirement is real and Virginia genuinely got there first, but K-8 delivery is integration into other subjects with no dedicated lesson, teacher or assessment. The page credits the policy, states the delivery model plainly, says explicitly that integration done well is genuinely good and that the problem is variance rather than ceiling, and gives parents a specific question to ask their own school instead of asserting a failure we cannot measure.

coding-classes-in-illinois.curriculumAuthority: Illinois computer science learning standards, written by the State Board of Education under HB 2170 and delivered by the end of 2021. The legal frame is an ENTITLEMENT to be offered a course, which is the page's spine: a floor, not a ceiling.
coding-classes-in-illinois.localProject: Chicago Data Portal beach water quality. Chicago Park District issues a swim advisory when predicted E. coli reaches at least 235 Colony Forming Units per 100 ml, and publishes lab data, advisories and model predictions daily through the season. Trap: CLASS IMBALANCE and the accuracy paradox. Advisories are rare, so a model that always answers safe scores about the same accuracy as a real one. Forces confusion matrix, precision and recall, and the judgement that a missed advisory and a false alarm are not equivalent harms. Sixth distinct KIND of error in the cluster.

sources.claim: HB 2170, the Education and Workforce Equity Act, was signed in March 2021 and championed by the Illinois Legislative Black Caucus. It requires schools to offer every student the opportunity to take at least one computer science course aligned to rigorous CS learning standards beginning in the 2023-2024 school year; requires ISBE to develop computer science learning standards, delivered by the end of 2021; requires districts to ensure students gain computer literacy skills starting in elementary school; and requires high school students to take one year of a course that includes intensive instruction in computer literacy beginning in the 2022-2023 school year.
sources.citation: Illinois HB 2170, Education and Workforce Equity Act, 2021

sources.claim: Chicago Public Schools made computer science a high school graduation requirement in 2016, ahead of the state and ahead of almost every large district in the United States.
sources.citation: Contemporaneous reporting on the CPS graduation requirement, 2016

sources.claim: The Chicago Park District monitors Lake Michigan beach water quality, testing for Escherichia coli as an indicator species, and a swim advisory is issued when the predicted E. coli level is at least 235 Colony Forming Units per 100 ml. The Chicago Data Portal publishes Beach E. coli Predictions, Beach Lab Data and Beach Swim Advisories, updated daily during the beach season. The City worked with the Park District, volunteer data scientists and university students on the forecasting model.
sources.citation: City of Chicago Data Portal, Beach E. coli Predictions

sources.claim: Illinois has 260,055 Indian Americans, 2.03 percent of the state population.

rejectedClaims.claim: An AP computer science course counts toward the three years of mathematics required for graduation in Illinois.
rejectedClaims.why: Widely reported but not confirmed at primary source, and the New Jersey lesson applies: a credential claim that resists sourcing gets stated as unconfirmed, never asserted. The page and its FAQ say plainly that we could not confirm it and direct families to their counsellor for the rule in force for their cohort.

coding-classes-in-new-york.curriculumAuthority: New York State Learning Standards for Computer Science and Digital Fluency, adopted by the Board of Regents in December 2020, full implementation expected by September 2024. Five concept areas, grade bands K-1, 2-3, 4-6, 7-8, 9-12. Distinctive because Cybersecurity is named as a top-level concept, which very few states do.
coding-classes-in-new-york.localProject: NYC Open Data 311 Service Requests, over 40 million rows by end of 2025, updated daily. Trap: rate versus count, the denominator problem. Ranking boroughs by raw noise complaints mostly ranks them by population. Second layer: a 311 record measures somebody choosing to report, not the event itself. Deliberately a fifth distinct KIND of error, and specifically NOT Texas's observation bias, which was about detection changing over time; this is about comparing groups of different sizes at one moment.

sources.claim: The Board of Regents adopted the New York State Learning Standards for Computer Science and Digital Fluency in December 2020, following a two-year statewide collaborative authoring, reviewing and revision process. Five concept areas: Impacts of Computing, Computational Thinking, Networks and System Design, Cybersecurity, and Digital Literacy. Standards are grouped into grade bands K-1, 2-3, 4-6, 7-8 and 9-12. All K-12 schools were expected to fully implement by September 2024.
sources.citation: New York State Education Department, Computer Science and Digital Fluency Learning Standards

sources.claim: On 4 November 2024 the State Education Department presented NY Inspires, implementing the Blue Ribbon Commission on Graduation Measures recommendations through four transformations: adopt the New York State Portrait of a Graduate, redefine credits, sunset diploma assessment requirements, and move to one diploma. Until specific changes are approved by the Board of Regents, current graduation requirements remain in effect for all public school students. Reporting has indicated the Regents exam requirement ending around the 2027-28 school year.
sources.citation: New York State Education Department, Current Diploma Requirements and the Graduation Measures Initiative

sources.claim: NYC Open Data publishes 311 Service Requests covering 2010 to the present, updated daily, split into a 2010-2019 historical set and a 2020-to-present set. As of December 2025 the data contained over 40 million rows. Each row includes complaint type, responding agency and geographic location.
sources.citation: NYC Open Data, 311 Service Requests

sources.claim: New York has 387,376 Indian Americans, 1.92 percent of the state population.
sources.citation: 2020 United States Census

sources.claim: The Hecht-Calandra Act of 1971 requires New York City to admit students to its specialized high schools solely on performance in the Specialized High Schools Admissions Test. The legislation originally covered Stuyvesant High School, the Bronx High School of Science and Brooklyn Technical High School. The SHSAT is the sole criterion for eight of the nine specialized high schools; the ninth, LaGuardia, admits by audition or portfolio.
sources.citation: New York Education Law, Hecht-Calandra Act 1971; NYC specialized high schools admissions

rejectedClaims.claim: New York students no longer need to pass Regents exams to graduate.
rejectedClaims.why: Premature. The direction is announced and the plan is published, but until the Board of Regents approves specific changes the current requirements remain in force for every public school student. The page states the plan, states plainly that nothing has changed yet, and tells families to confirm the position for their child's cohort with the school.

coding-classes-in-california.curriculumAuthority: California Computer Science Standards, adopted by the State Board of Education on 6 September 2018. Six core concepts and seven core practices, aligned to the K-12 Computer Science Framework. Crucially VOLUNTARY, which is the page's central fact and the sharpest contrast with New Jersey and Texas.
coding-classes-in-california.localProject: CAL FIRE incident acreage. Trap: heavy-tailed distribution defeating a summary statistic. In 2020 nearly 10,000 fires burned over 4.2 million acres, a mean near 400 acres per fire, but the August Complex alone exceeded one million acres, close to a quarter of the season, while most fires were tiny. The mean describes no actual fire and no arithmetic error exists anywhere. Comparing mean acreage across years mostly measures whether a megafire happened. Deliberately a fourth distinct KIND of error: New Jersey metric definition, Ontario model misspecification, Texas observation bias, California summary statistics on a heavy tail.
requiredMentions: six core concepts and seven core practices

sources.claim: The State Board of Education adopted California's first K-12 computer science standards on 6 September 2018. They are built on six core computer science concepts and seven core practices, aligned to the K-12 Computer Science Framework, and developed with input from CSTA, NSF-funded work and industry. They are voluntary, intended to give substantive guidance while allowing flexibility across local education agencies to decide how best to incorporate computer science based on local capacity and context.
sources.citation: California Department of Education, Computer Science Content Standards

sources.claim: UC subject requirement Area D asks for two years of laboratory science providing fundamental knowledge in at least two of biology, chemistry and physics, with a third year recommended. Computer science, engineering and applied science courses can be used in Area D as an additional science, that is a third year and beyond, not toward the core two years. Area G is one year of college-preparatory elective. Courses must be approved by UC and appear on the school's a-g course list.
sources.citation: University of California, A-G subject requirements, Subject Area D: Science

sources.claim: In the 2020 California fire season nearly 10,000 fires burned over 4.2 million acres, the largest wildfire season in California's modern recorded history. The August Complex exceeded one million acres, described as the first gigafire, formed from around 30 separate lightning-caused fires in the Mendocino National Forest that converged.
sources.citation: CAL FIRE 2020 incident archive; contemporaneous reporting on the 2020 fire siege

sources.claim: California has 830,259 Indian Americans, 2.1 percent of the state population, the largest such population of any US state in absolute terms.
sources.citation: 2020 United States Census

rejectedClaims.claim: Computer science counts as a laboratory science for University of California admission.
rejectedClaims.why: Half true and therefore dangerous. It counts only as an ADDITIONAL science, third year and beyond, and does not replace the required two years drawn from biology, chemistry and physics. A student who plans as though it substitutes arrives in Grade 12 short. The page states the distinction explicitly and contrasts it with the Texas LOTE rule, which genuinely is a substitution.

coding-classes-in-texas.curriculumAuthority: Technology Applications TEKS, revised by the State Board of Education in 2022, implemented from the 2024-25 school year. Five strands, with computational thinking the largest departure from the 2011 standards.
coding-classes-in-texas.localProject: NOAA Storm Prediction Center tornado records for Texas. Trap: observation bias. Reported counts climb since 1950, but population spread, the 1990s Doppler radar rollout and the 2007 switch from the Fujita to the Enhanced Fujita scale all changed detection. NOAA's own assessment is that removing F/EF0 counts nearly eliminates the annual frequency trend. Method taught: find a subset whose collection method did not change (strong tornadoes) and see whether the trend survives. Deliberately a different KIND of error from New Jersey (metric definition) and Ontario (model misspecification).
requiredMentions: Computer Science I, II and III

sources.claim: 19 TAC 74.12 Languages Other Than English, two credits: 'The credits may be selected from the following: (i) any two levels in the same language, including comparable AP or IB language courses that do not count toward another credit required for graduation; or (ii) two credits in computer programming languages, including computer coding, to be selected from Computer Science I, II, and III, AP Computer Science Principles, AP Computer Science A, IB Computer Science Standard Level, and IB Computer Science Higher Level.' A separate provision covers a student who cannot complete a second LOTE credit, requiring agreement from the LOTE teacher, the principal or designee and the parent, or the ARD committee, or the Section 504 committee. NOTE the copy consulted is marked effective until 2025-08-01 and TEA issued an August 2025 update to Chapter 74 Subchapter B; the page tells families to confirm the current text.
sources.citation: 19 Tex. Admin. Code section 74.12, Foundation High School Program

sources.claim: Technology Applications TEKS were revised in 2022 and implemented from the 2024-25 school year. Five strands: computational thinking; creativity and innovation; data literacy, management, and representation; digital citizenship; and practical technology concepts. Computational thinking breaks problem solving into decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction and algorithms. The 2022 revision gave each grade K to 5 its own standards instead of grade bands.
sources.citation: Texas Education Agency, Technology Applications; SBOE April 2022 adoption

sources.claim: The Foundation High School Program requires at least 22 credits; an endorsement takes the total to 26. Subject minimums include English 4, Mathematics 3, Science 3, Social Studies 3, Languages Other Than English 2, Physical Education 1, Fine Arts 1 and Electives 5. Endorsement options are STEM, business and industry, public services, arts and humanities, and multidisciplinary studies. The Distinguished Level of Achievement requires 26 credits including Algebra II.
sources.citation: Texas Education Agency, Graduation Toolkit 2025

sources.claim: Inconsistencies in the NOAA severe events database arise from changes in population awareness, reporting practices, Doppler radar technology and NWS guidelines, which have likely introduced artificial trends. Removing F/EF0 counts from the database nearly eliminates the annual frequency trend. The 2007 change from the Fujita to the Enhanced Fujita scale produced large increases in weak tornado reports.
sources.citation: NOAA State of the Science Fact Sheet: Tornadoes, Climate Variability and Climate Change, September 2023

sources.claim: Texas has 480,566 Indian Americans, 1.65 percent of the state population, the second largest such population of any US state.
sources.citation: 2020 United States Census

rejectedClaims.claim: A Texas student needs district or principal approval to use computer science for the LOTE requirement.
rejectedClaims.why: This confuses two separate provisions of 19 TAC 74.12. Clause (ii) is an unconditional listed alternative needing no permission. The named-approval process belongs to the different provision covering a student who has begun a language and is unlikely to complete the second credit. The page explains both and distinguishes them, because families are routinely quoted the wrong one.

coding-classes-in-ontario.curriculumAuthority: Ontario mathematics curriculum, Grades 1 to 8 (2020). Six strands, with coding placed inside the Algebra strand rather than taught as a separate subject. Ontario was the first province in Canada to do this.
coding-classes-in-ontario.localProject: IESO hourly Ontario electricity demand against temperature. Trap: the relationship is V-shaped, because Ontario heats in winter and cools in summer. A single straight-line fit returns a near-zero correlation and invites the student to conclude that temperature does not drive electricity demand, which is spectacularly wrong. The fix is to model two regimes, or to use heating and cooling degree days. This is a model-misspecification trap, deliberately a different KIND of error from the metric-definition trap used on the New Jersey page.
requiredMentions: Social-Emotional Learning Skills and Mathematical Processes
Digital Technology and Innovations in the Changing World

sources.claim: The 2020 Ontario Grades 1 to 8 mathematics curriculum has six strands: Number, Algebra, Data, Spatial Sense, Financial Literacy, and Social-Emotional Learning Skills and Mathematical Processes. Coding sits inside the Algebra strand. Grade 1 students write code to order a sequence of steps; Grade 2 develop code to move multiple objects from one location on a grid to another; Grade 3 write code to perform a repeating operation such as a repeating add 3; Grade 4 write and read code to create geometric designs.
sources.citation: Government of Ontario, mathematics curriculum Grades 1 to 8, effective 2020

sources.claim: OSSD requires a minimum of 30 credits. Students entering Grade 9 in 2023 or earlier need 18 compulsory and 12 optional; those entering in 2024-25 onwards need 17 compulsory and 13 optional. All cohorts must earn at least two of the 30 credits online. Students must meet the literacy graduation requirement via the OSSLT, the OSSLC, or an adjudication process, and complete 40 hours of community involvement activities.
sources.citation: Ontario Schools, Kindergarten to Grade 12: Policy and Program Requirements, section 6

sources.claim: Starting in the 2026-2027 school year, students who enter Grade 9 in 2025-2026 and onwards must meet a Financial Literacy Graduation Requirement, achieving a mark of 70 percent or higher on the financial literacy modules.
sources.citation: Ontario Schools, Kindergarten to Grade 12: Policy and Program Requirements, section 6

sources.claim: The IESO Data Directory publishes Ontario demand and market demand for each hour, plus hourly electricity consumption aggregated by Forward Sortation Area, which is the first three characters of a postal code. It also publishes the Hourly Ontario Energy Price.
sources.citation: Independent Electricity System Operator, Data Directory

sources.claim: Ontario secondary computer studies runs on The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 10 to 12: Computer Studies, revised 2008. Course codes: ICS3U (Grade 11 university preparation), ICS3C (Grade 11 college preparation), ICS4U (Grade 12 university preparation), ICS4C (Grade 12 college preparation). The Grade 10 course ICS2O was replaced from September 2023 by ICD2O, Digital Technology and Innovations in the Changing World. ICS3U and ICS4U remain on the 2008 revision.
sources.citation: Ontario Ministry of Education, The Ontario Curriculum Grades 10 to 12: Computer Studies, 2008 Revised

sources.claim: New Jersey state minimum graduation requirements total 120 credits. Mathematics 15 credits including Algebra I, Geometry and a third year building on them. There is no computer science credit line in the state minimum.

sources.claim: NJSLS-CSDT covers Kindergarten through grade 12. coding-classes-in-brunei.curriculumAuthority: SPN21, Brunei's National Education System for the 21st Century, administered by the Ministry of Education. Secondary runs Year 7 to Year 11: Years 7 and 8 are lower secondary ending in the Student Progress Assessment, and Years 9 to 11 are upper secondary ending in the Brunei-Cambridge GCE Ordinary Level, a qualification jointly branded with Cambridge rather than a purely national one. A learner may opt for a shorter two years of upper secondary instead of three, subject to evaluation of their lower secondary academic record. THE SPINE OF THIS PAGE IS NOT THE CURRICULUM, it is the calendar: Ministry of Finance and Economy division listings state working days as Monday to Thursday and Saturday, Friday varies by division and Sunday appears on none of them, so Saturday is a working day and Brunei is widely described as the only country with a non-contiguous working week. coding-classes-in-brunei.localProject: The weekend is an input, not a constant. Every mainstream date library, spreadsheet function and tutorial hardcodes Saturday and Sunday, usually not even as a parameter. The fix reframes the function: the set of non-working days stops being a constant inside the code and becomes an argument passed in, which forces the caller to know it, which forces somebody to ask. In Brunei asking is unavoidable because the answer differs between a government household and an oil-sector one, so one program yields two correct answers depending on an input the original version did not have. Distinct from every other page in the cluster: this is a genuine hardcoded-locale bug rather than a statistical misreading, and it is the only page whose trap the market's own calendar creates. Its subject is the administrative shape of the capital. Bandar Seri Begawan sits in Brunei-Muara, the smallest and most populous of the four districts at 332,462 residents. The municipality is estimated at 72,133 people and is composed of THIRTEEN mukims: Berakas 'A', Berakas 'B', Burong Pingai Ayer, Gadong 'A', Gadong 'B', Kianggeh, Kilanas, Kota Batu, Peramu, Saba, Sungai Kebun, Sungai Kedayan and Tamoi. SIX of those thirteen are Kampong Ayer, the stilt settlement over the Brunei River, and both mukim lists were cross-checked so the subset relation is exact. Awang Semaun Secondary School is described as the only school of its kind whose buildings are built on water. coding-classes-in-bandar-seri-begawan.localProject: You cannot add a part to its whole. The learner is asked how many people live in the capital and its water village, given 72,133 for the city and 10,250 for Kampong Ayer at the 2016 census, and almost everybody adds them to 82,383. But Kampong Ayer's six mukims are six of the capital's thirteen, so the smaller set is entirely contained in the larger, the intersection IS the smaller set, and the union collapses to 72,133. The addition overstated by exactly 10,250, which is 14.2 per cent. The rule taken away: before adding two counts, name one person who is in the first and not the second; if you cannot describe that person the sets are nested and addition is a category error whose size depends on the overlap rather than on the magnitude of the numbers. The extension turns the same discipline on the two census columns: the total falls 10,250 to 8,902 between 2016 and 2021, about 13 per cent, yet two of the six mukims RISE (Peramu 1,111 to 1,151, Sungai Kedayan 230 to 241), so a direction true of a total can be false of its parts. Every mukim figure was fetched from that mukim's own record and the 2016 column sums exactly to the reported 10,250. Distinct from every other page: this is set membership, not a boundary definition and not a statistical misreading.

coding-classes-in-temburong.localProject: The network changed, not the map. A learner writes a travel-time program from coordinates and straight-line distance, which passes on a dozen town pairs, then runs it on Bangar and Bandar Seri Begawan for 2019 and for 2021. Assigned to this page and no other: checked against the stable-identifier trap on Ash Sharqiyah North, the visits-against-visitors trap on Al Khuwair and the missing-as-zero trap on Ibra before it was chosen.

sources.claim: Al Suwaiq Industrial City total area of 10 million square metres, inaugurated 2024, targeting food and beverage, pharmaceutical and logistics sectors.

Disley Private School describes itself as the only Cambridge accredited bilingual school in Al Suwaiq, working within the Ministry of Education framework combined with the Cambridge International Curriculum.

The wilayat contains 32 villages including Al Nabrah, Al Mabrah, Al Tharmad, Al Hailain, Al Manfash and Bawarh; it measures roughly 48 km by 80 km and is the largest wilayat in Oman; Al Suwaiq Fort is 60 m by 43 m with three circular towers and one square, restored 1992.
Pakistan School Suwaiq has served the Pakistani community and other expatriate families in As Suwaiq since 1994.

rejectedClaims: A headline population for the wilayat. One published table gives about 200,994 at the 2022 census and the wilayat article gives about 140,577 for 2021. The two could not be reconciled at primary source, so no population figure appears on the page and the National Centre for Statistics and Information is named as the authority.

A count of agricultural villages. One secondary source says the wilayat oversees about 46 agricultural villages while the wilayat article counts 32 villages in total. The page uses only the 32 figure and does not repeat the 46.

coding-classes-in-saham.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma, delivered in government schools across the wilayat. The page argues from distance rather than from curriculum: Saham is about 200 kilometres from Muscat, so the weekly cost of a physical class is a day rather than an evening, and that is the honest case for live online delivery.
coding-classes-in-saham.localProject: A number living inside a text label. Numbered outlet labels across two of Saham's named aflaj, sorted plainly, putting 10 before 2 and moving five of six positions. Assigned to this page and no other: natural sort was checked free against every page in the cluster before it was chosen, unlike the identifier and count-distinct traps which are already taken.

sources.claim: Saham is a coastal town in Al Batinah North between Al Khaburah and Sohar, about 200 km from Muscat; main industries are fishing and farming; the souq was renovated to modern standards in 2018 and holds a livestock market on the seventh day of Dhu al-Hijja; named regions include Majaz, Al-Huwail, Al-Marfa, Al-Hadeeb, Al-Gowaisa, Al-Deel and Hafeet, and the khors Khor Al Milh, Khor AlHimam and Khor AlShiyadi.

Saham souq covers 130,000 square metres; the slaughterhouse opened in 2015; the aflaj Bani Ameer, Al Roodha, Al Mahab and Sheidah and the wadis Aheen, Khour Al Malh and Al Sakahn are named; Al Souq Fort was once the residence of the governor; villages include Sur Al Shiyadi, Sur Al Buloosh, Mukhaileef, Khour Al Hamam and Al Manqel.
Saham is recorded as one of the larger wilayats of Al Batinah North and sits between Al Khaboura and Sohar on the Sea of Oman coast, with lemon production historically exported in quantity.

rejectedClaims: A headline population. Three published figures exist on three different bases: 147,775 for 2017, 165,546 at the 2022 census, and about 122,493 for 2023 on an Omani-citizens-only series. Mixing bases would be worse than omitting the number, so no population appears on the page.

Any statement about the real rotation order of a named falaj. The four falaj names are published; their water shares are not ours to publish, and the outlet numbers in the project are labelled as teaching values.

coding-classes-in-al-amarat.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma, delivered through the 30 schools the wilayat records for more than 25,000 students. The page argues from access rather than curriculum: Al Amarat sits behind a mountain range from Bausher on a road its own residents have campaigned to replace, so a weekly class that depends on that corridor is a weekly risk.
coding-classes-in-al-amarat.localProject: Percentages that are each rounded correctly and do not total 100. Twenty shares across the wilayat's 20 published administrative areas total 100.2 under independent rounding, and largest-remainder apportionment returns them to 100.0 by moving two figures. Assigned to this page and no other: checked against the weighted-average trap on Al Batinah North and Mawaleh, the percentage-wording trap on Al Ghubrah and the base-rate trap on Duqm before it was chosen.

sources.claim: Al Amarat comprises 20 administrative areas, contains 57 valleys and 61 aflaj, produces dates, mangoes and sidr, operates seven factories for plaster and brick, and contains Beit Al Maqam Fort.
30 schools provide educational services to more than 25 thousand students.
Residents have called for a permanent solution to the Amerat-Bausher mountain road, with many arguing that an alternative route, especially a tunnel, is required to connect the two wilayats.
Muscat Governorate consists of six wilayats: Muscat, Muttrah, Al Seeb, Qurayat, Bausher and Al Amerat.

rejectedClaims: The wilayat area. One source gives 925 square kilometres for Al Amarat and another gives the same 925 for Liwa in Al Batinah North. Those cannot both be right as stated, so neither page carries an area and both name the National Centre for Statistics and Information as the authority.

A single headline population. Published figures range from about 69,132 in a 2016 breakdown to roughly 139,755 at the 2022 census, and one secondary source prints "121,103 thousand people", which cannot be right on any reading. The page states the range with both years attached rather than picking one figure.

That the Wadi Adai to Al Amerat link is a tunnel. It is a mountain road corridor. Residents have argued a tunnel is what is needed, which is a call rather than a built fact, and the page words it that way.

coding-classes-in-rustaq.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page does not argue from curriculum at all. It argues that Rustaq already runs a scheduling system older than the word, with fixed slots, a repeating cycle, an elected administrator and an audit role, so a learner here does not need the concept explained, only the notation.
coding-classes-in-rustaq.localProject: Modular arithmetic on a repeating cycle. A 48-athar day inside an eight day dawaran is 384 turns; naive division places 8 of them on the wrong day and its worst answer is day 9 of an eight day cycle. Assigned to this page and no other: modulo and cyclic scheduling were checked free across every page in the cluster, and the elapsed-time trap already used by Ibri and Nizwa was avoided deliberately.

sources.claim: Falaj Al-Muyassar is one of the five aflaj UNESCO inscribed in 2006, is a Dawoodi falaj reaching 50 metres depth with a flow of 210 litres per second, and is among the most significant aflaj in Wilayat Al Rustaq.

Falaj water is shared by athar of 30 minutes on a rotation, the dawaran, typically of 7 to 14 days; a baddah is 12 hours or 24 athar; the falaj is run by an elected wakil with arifs regulating timing and a qabidh keeping financial records, and night timing is read from known stars.

Al Rustaq Fort dates to the 13th century and was expanded by the Ya'aruba dynasty between 1624 and 1649, with four towers the tallest over 18 metres; Al Hazm Castle was built by Imam Sultan bin Saif al Yarubi in the early 18th century; Wadi Al Hoqain lies 45 km from the centre with year-round streams and Niyabat Al Hoqain about 150 km from Muscat.

Ain Al Kasfa lies about 1,500 metres west of Rustaq Castle, irrigates the surrounding palm farms, and carries the largest water volume of any spring in northern Oman; an Abbasid governor tried to bury it and the water reappeared about ten metres from the original source.

rejectedClaims: The actual rotation order or share allocation of Falaj Al-Muyassar or any other named falaj. Shares belong to the shareholders and are not published; the eight day cycle in the project is chosen from inside the documented seven to fourteen day range and is labelled as such on the page.
A population figure for the wilayat. The 2022 census gives about 129,050, but this page makes no argument that depends on it, so it is not stated rather than stated decoratively.

coding-classes-in-jalan-bani-bu-ali.market: Jalan Bani Bu Ali, Ash Sharqiyah South
coding-classes-in-jalan-bani-bu-ali.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from currency rather than curriculum: the Omani rial divides into 1000 baisa, so every price in this trading town carries three decimal places, and the two-decimal money advice that dominates programming writing is a digit short before it starts.
coding-classes-in-jalan-bani-bu-ali.localProject: Money in binary floating point, in a three decimal currency. A six line Friday souq basket totals 11.325000000000001 as a float against 11.325 exactly, prints as 11.325 either way, and fails the equality check a till runs at closing. Counting the same money in whole baisa passes. Assigned to this page and no other: floating point money was checked free across every page in the cluster before it was chosen.

sources.claim: Jami Al-Hamoda in Jalan Bani Bu Ali has 52 separate mud-brick domes of equal size with a falaj running beneath it, openings called mabariq, 24 cylinders, five corridors, capacity for more than 700 worshippers, was built almost 500 years ago, and is locally called Al Qibab or the Mosque of Domes.

Jalan Bani Bu Ali is a commercial town and tourist destination in Ash Sharqiyah South with many shops and supermarkets, a traditional souq about 1 km south of the centre trading on Friday mornings, sand dunes with standing water pools, a distinct summer rainy season unusual for Oman, and was the site of an 1821 British East India Company expedition.
The mosque is located in the Wilayat of Jalan Bani Bu Ali in Ash Sharqiyah South Governorate and serves as a centre for study and preservation of the Holy Qur'an.

rejectedClaims: An exact founding date for Jami Al-Hamoda. Sources say it was built almost 500 years ago, which is an approximation, and the page repeats it as an approximation rather than converting it into a year.
A population figure. The 2022 census gives about 117,730 for the wilayat, but no argument on this page depends on it, so it is omitted rather than used as decoration.

coding-classes-in-al-musanaah.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the wilayat's sporting infrastructure rather than its schools: Al Musanaah hosts international championship sailing, so results here are recorded under published rules that anybody can check, which is what lets the project show a right answer beside a wrong one instead of asserting which is which.
coding-classes-in-al-musanaah.localProject: A missing value inside an aggregate, in a sport that already ruled on it. A six race series where a boat sailing four races comes first on an average that skips the blanks and last under World Sailing's low point rule of entries plus one. Assigned to this page and no other: deliberately distinct from Ibra's missing-as-zero trap, because skipping is the more dangerous failure and produces a plausible answer where zeroing produces an obviously silly one.

sources.claim: Al-Musannah Sports City covers 1,000,000 square metres with capacity for 5,000 athletes, was built between 2008 and 2010 and opened on 8 December 2010, hosting the opening ceremony of the second Asian Beach Games held from 8 to 16 December 2010.

The inaugural World Sailing Inclusion Championships were held at Mussanah from 30 November to 8 December 2025 with 154 athletes entered, across four classes: Hansa 303, RS Venture Connect, ILCA 6 and FarEast 28R.

The Asian Sailing Federation selected Oman Sail's Mussanah Sailing School as a High Performance Centre; the school sits at the marina and water sports centre at the Barcelo Mussanah Resort about 85 km north of Muscat, with a 20 metre wide slipway, a boatyard and docking for around 400 boats.

Al-Musannah is a coastal town in Al Batinah South Governorate with a 2020 census population of 99,204, one of six wilayats in the governorate alongside Rustaq, Al Awabi, Nakhal, Wadi Al Maawil and Barka.

rejectedClaims: Any claim that the race series in the project is a real regatta result. It is a teaching example and the page labels it as one. Only the scoring rule is real.

Attendance or entry figures for events at the venue beyond the 154 athletes reported for the 2025 championships. Other event totals could not be confirmed at first-party source and are therefore not stated.

coding-classes-in-bahla.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from distance and from subject rather than from curriculum: Bahla is about 200 kilometres from Muscat and 40 from Nizwa, and its published record is unusually full of measurements of awkwardly shaped things, which is the case data work handles worst.
coding-classes-in-bahla.localProject: Perimeter against area, and its software cousin the bounding box. Twelve kilometres of oasis wall enclosing anywhere from 11.46 to 0.30 square kilometres depending on shape, a spread of 39 times, and an eight-vertex plot whose bounding box area is 98.6 per cent too big against the shoelace formula. Assigned to this page and no other. The obvious Bahla hook was the Nabhani dates in AH and AD, which was rejected because Nizwa forty kilometres away already owns calendar conversion.

sources.claim: Bahla Fort was the first site in Oman inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, in 1987; it covers about 9,822 square metres, is irregular in shape, and the oasis walls around it extend for more than 12 kilometres.

Bahla lies about 40 km from Nizwa and 200 km from Muscat at about 550 m elevation; the fort is 13th century with adobe walls and towers on stone foundations inside a 12 km fortified wall; the Nabhani dynasty ruled from the mid 12th to the end of the 15th century with Bahla as second and later main capital; pottery is dated back as early as 2500 BC; Jabrin Castle lies 5 km south west, built under Al Ya'ruba in the mid 17th century; the Friday Mosque carries a sculpted mihrab of roughly the 14th century.
Bahla Fort is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, reference 433.

rejectedClaims: A headline population. One source gives 85,000 and the 2022 census table gives 96,415, and no argument on this page depends on either, so neither is stated.

A precise date for the Friday Mosque mihrab. The record says approximately the 14th century and the page keeps the approximation rather than converting it into a year that would read better and mean less.

coding-classes-in-al-mudhaibi.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from scale rather than curriculum: Al Mudhaibi is the largest wilayat in its governorate at roughly 3,000 square kilometres with two niabas and settlements of wildly unequal size, so no single physical location could serve it and no careless average can describe it.
coding-classes-in-al-mudhaibi.localProject: The average of several rates against the overall rate. Five settlements, four small and one holding 91 per cent of the learners: the mean of the five rates is 77.0 per cent and total passes over total entries is 57.5, a gap of 19.5 percentage points. Assigned to this page and no other: checked free across the cluster, and kept clear of the percentage-wording trap on Al Ghubrah and the share-rounding trap on Al Amarat.

sources.claim: Al Mudhaibi is the largest wilayat in Ash Sharqiyah with an estimated area of about 3,000 square kilometres, holds the two niabas Sinaw and Samad Ash Shan, and its villages include Al Sudairah, Barzman, Al Zahib, Al Alia, Bani Difaa and the Al-Dhaqiq area between Lazq and Al Maysar; agriculture is the first craft, with palm, lemon, alfalfa and vegetables.
Samad al-Shan is noted for ancient Umm al-Nar period sites dated to roughly 2500 to 2000 BCE.
Suq Sinaw is among the most popular souqs in Oman, selling dresses, khanjars and jewellery.

rejectedClaims: A population figure. The 2022 census gives about 92,193 for the wilayat, but the page argues from area and from the inequality between settlements rather than from a total, so a headline population would be decoration.
Any real per-settlement pass rate. No public per-village result file exists, so the counts in the project are teaching values and are labelled as such on the page.

coding-classes-in-al-khaburah.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from dispersion rather than curriculum: 198 villages spread from the coast to Adh Dhahirah and about 176 kilometres from Muscat means no physical centre could be convenient for more than a handful of them.
coding-classes-in-al-khaburah.localProject: The sum of the peaks against the peak of the sums. A modelled year across the wilayat's 198 villages, each with its own busy season: summing the individual peaks overstates the real system maximum by about 100 per cent, and zero of the 198 villages peaked on the day the whole wilayat did. Assigned to this page and no other; checked free across the cluster before it was chosen.

sources.claim: Al Khaburah has 198 villages including Al Sihra, Al Qala, Khadra Al Makatim, Sanaa Bani Ghafir and Miha Bani Kayoum; it lies about 176 km from Muscat and stretches from Saham in the north to As Suwaiq in the south and Adh Dhahirah in the west; residents work in agriculture, sheep herding, fishing, khanjar making, weaving, pottery, copper and leather.
Al Khabourah Castle is the most famous of the wilayat's forts and castles and dates to the 19th century AD.
Al Khaburah is a wilayat of Al Batinah North Governorate in Oman.

rejectedClaims: A population figure. The 2022 census gives about 89,971, but the page argues from the village count and their independence rather than from a total, so a headline population would be decoration.
Any real per-village demand or consumption figure. No public daily record exists, so the series in the project are modelled and are labelled as modelled on the page.

coding-classes-in-shinas.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the border rather than the curriculum: Shinas overlooks some of the Sultanate's most important land crossings and runs a port trading with Iran, so its records are bilingual by necessity and its software has to hold two scripts rather than one.
coding-classes-in-shinas.localProject: A field measured in characters against a field measured in bytes. Place names from the wilayat in Latin and Arabic through a twenty byte limit: every Latin name survives, a fourteen character Arabic name loses three letters, and a twenty character Arabic name loses half. Assigned to this page and no other; checked free across the cluster before it was chosen.

sources.claim: Shinas is one of the six coastal wilayats of Al Batinah North, bordered to the north by the United Arab Emirates and overlooking some of the Sultanate's most important land crossings, with fertile agricultural plains using aflaj irrigation.
Shinas Port handled 88,000 tonnes over a twelve month period, mainly building materials, food, live animals and chemical and pharmaceutical products traded between Oman and Iran.
Traditional dhows still sail from Shinas and fresh fish is caught for supply to local markets.

rejectedClaims: A population figure. The 2022 census gives about 88,317, but the page argues from the border position and the bilingual record rather than from a total.
Any claim about the port's capacity or its peak throughput. The 88,000 tonne figure is a twelve month throughput, and the page says so rather than letting it be read as a capacity.

coding-classes-in-samail.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the shape of the wilayat rather than from curriculum: 55 settlements strung along a wadi that divides the Hajar into two ranges means no single meeting point is convenient for most of them.
coding-classes-in-samail.localProject: The header row counted as data. A list of the wilayat's 55 villages read without skipping the first line yields 56, one of them named village; the mosque total stays correct at 388 either way and the average per village moves from 7.05 to 6.93. Assigned to this page and no other; checked free across the cluster before it was chosen.

sources.claim: Samail lies in Ad Dakhiliyah beside the Hajar Mountains; Wadi Samail is one of the largest wadis and the Samail Gap divides the Hajar into eastern and western subranges; the wilayat holds 55 villages and towns and more than 300 mosques.
The Mazin bin Ghadouba Mosque in Samail is considered the oldest mosque in Oman and was built by Mazin bin Ghadouba in 627 AD.
Mazin bin Ghadouba is recorded as the first Muslim in Oman and the mosque is described as the first mosque of Oman.

rejectedClaims: A headline population. One source gives about 40,000 for the wilayat and the 2022 census table gives about 87,997. The two could not be reconciled, so no population appears and the page argues from the settlement count instead.
Any per-village mosque figure. Only the wilayat totals are published, so the per-village numbers in the project are teaching values and are labelled as such.

coding-classes-in-izki.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the length of the record rather than from curriculum: a falaj with more than two millennia behind it is the clearest case anywhere of observations that were never evenly sampled.
coding-classes-in-izki.localProject: Readings taken at irregular intervals, averaged as though evenly spaced. Six falaj readings across fifty four years, five of them in the first five: the plain mean is 87.7 and the time weighted mean is 95.2 on the same six numbers. Assigned to this page and no other; checked free across the cluster, and kept clear of the elapsed-time work on Ibri and the seasonality work on Salalah.

sources.claim: Izki is popularly claimed to be the oldest town in Oman and was notorious for intrigues between the Yamani and the Nizari; the Yamani are southern Arabs claiming origins in Yemen who migrated to Oman between the 2nd century BC and the 2nd century AD, and the Nizari are northern Arabs who migrated from what is now the Nejd.

Izki is celebrated as Oman's oldest city on the evidence of its ancient aflaj and the twin walled towns of Izki or al-Yemen and al-Nizar; Falaj al Malaki is one of the five largest aflaj in Oman with a history spanning over two millennia.
Al Malki Falaj is shared by Nazar village and is one of the important water sources in the area; Harat Al Yemen is the old quarter walked by visitors.

rejectedClaims: That Izki IS the oldest town in Oman. The sources say popularly claimed and celebrated as, which is a claim about a reputation rather than a settled dating, and the page repeats it in those terms.

A population figure and any real flow series for the falaj. The 2022 census gives about 66,034 for the wilayat, which nothing here argues from, and no public flow record exists, so the project readings are labelled as teaching values.

coding-classes-in-liwa.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from a documented naming discrepancy rather than from curriculum: the largest facility in the wilayat carries the neighbouring wilayat's name in its own published description, which makes it the clearest available case of a location that cannot be inferred from a label.
coding-classes-in-liwa.localProject: Deriving a location from a name. Five records through a name-based wilayat guess: two are misfiled, and because the port is the only row carrying weight, a million tonnes a week moves from Liwa to Sohar with nothing raised. Assigned to this page and no other; distinct from the stable-identifier work on Ash Sharqiyah North because this is about inferring an ATTRIBUTE from a name rather than about the identity of the key itself.
requiredMentions: National Centre for Statistics and Information

sources.claim: SOHAR Port and Freezone is a deep sea port and adjacent free zone located in Liwa, Al Batinah North, despite the name suggesting otherwise, and the port handles over one million tonnes of sea cargo each week and around 3,500 ships a year.
Liwa is a wilayat of Al Batinah North lying north of Sohar and overlooking the Gulf of Oman to its east, distributed over 51 villages.
From the towers of Liwa Fort a visitor can see many of the wilayat's villages, including the coastal village of Harmul and its mangrove trees.

rejectedClaims: The wilayat area. Two published sources give 925 square kilometres for Liwa and the same 925 for Al Amarat in Muscat Governorate, which cannot both be right as stated. Neither page states an area, and both name the National Centre for Statistics and Information as the authority.
A population figure. The 2022 census gives about 63,292, but the page argues from the naming discrepancy rather than from a total.

coding-classes-in-qurayyat.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from inequality of scale rather than curriculum: a fishing coast running from a town fleet down to three boat landings is the clearest available case of why a percentage ranking rewards being small rather than being busy.
coding-classes-in-qurayyat.localProject: A rate computed on a tiny denominator. Four landing points given one extra boat each: the three boat harbour posts 33.3 per cent, the town posts 0.6, and the town would need about sixty more boats to match the headline. Assigned to this page and no other; distinct from the share-rounding trap on Al Amarat and the average-of-rates trap on Al Mudhaibi because this is about the size of the base rather than the method of aggregation.

sources.claim: The Bimmah Sinkhole is in the Dabab area of Wilayat Qurayyat on the northeast coast of Muscat Governorate, about 600 metres inland, is a pool about 65 feet deep confirmed by geologists as a sinkhole though local legend holds a meteorite made it, and holds fresh and salt water in roughly equal proportions giving it a turquoise hue.
Quriyat is known for its traditional fishing boats and views over the sea, and its past was marked by fierce resistance to Portuguese invasion; it is today described as a quiet fishing village.
Muscat Governorate consists of six wilayats: Muscat, Muttrah, Al Seeb, Qurayat, Bausher and Al Amerat.

rejectedClaims: That a meteorite formed the Bimmah Sinkhole. Geologists have confirmed it is a sinkhole; the meteorite account is a local legend and the page presents it as one rather than choosing between them silently.

A population figure and any real per-landing-point boat count. The 2022 census gives about 63,006 for the wilayat, which nothing here argues from, and no public boat record exists, so the project counts are labelled as teaching values.

coding-classes-in-jalan-bani-bu-hassan.market: Jalan Bani Bu Hassan, Ash Sharqiyah South
coding-classes-in-jalan-bani-bu-hassan.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the wilayat's own name rather than from curriculum: it and its neighbour differ only in the final word, and its fort answers to two names, so it carries both halves of the key problem at once in a way no invented example could.
coding-classes-in-jalan-bani-bu-hassan.localProject: A key built by squashing and truncating a name. Sweeping the width from eight to fourteen characters across Jalan Bani Bu Hassan and Jalan Bani Bu Ali: they collide at every width up to eleven and separate at twelve, so one character is the entire safety margin. Paired with the reverse fault, one fort under two names. Assigned to this page and no other; distinct from the stable-identifier work on Ash Sharqiyah North because this is about the WIDTH of a derived key rather than about choosing one.

sources.claim: Jalan Bani Bu Hassan Fort, sometimes also known as Al Muhaywil Castle, is in Ash Sharqiyah South; it is said to have been founded in the 9th century during the reign of Al-Muhanna bin Jayfar as Imam of Oman, was thoroughly rebuilt during the reign of Thuwaini bin Said, Sultan from 1856 to 1866, and served as the main fortification in the area and the home and office of the local wali.
Jalan Bani Bu Hassan is a wilayat of Ash Sharqiyah South Governorate in Oman.
Ash Sharqiyah South contains the wilayats Sur, Jalan Bani Bu Ali, Jalan Bani Bu Hassan, Al Kamil Wal Wafi and Masirah.

rejectedClaims: A firm 9th century founding date for the fort. The sources say it is said to have been founded then, which is a tradition rather than a dated record, and the page keeps that wording. The 1856 to 1866 reign under which it was rebuilt is the firmer date and the page leans on that one.
A population figure. The 2022 census gives about 50,755 for the wilayat, but the page argues entirely from the names rather than from any total.

coding-classes-in-bidiyah.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the shape of the wilayat rather than from curriculum: a settlement that works as the entrance to a sand sea is a route rather than a centre, and teaching that travels to the learner is the only arrangement that treats the whole route alike.
coding-classes-in-bidiyah.localProject: A threshold stored as a value. Twelve dune heights capped at 100 because the source said over 100 metres: the mean falls from 97.8 to 84.7, the maximum from 156 to 100, the standard deviation from 33.6 to 19.9, and the count of dunes above 100 metres falls from six to zero. Assigned to this page and no other; checked free across the cluster before it was chosen.

sources.claim: Bidiya is a wilayat of North Al Sharqiyah about 230 kilometres southeast of Muscat, holding plains, mountains, dunes, oases, aflaj and natural springs, and sitting on the edge of the Wahiba Sands.
Dunes in the Wahiba Sands rise over 100 metres high, and the sand sea covers roughly 1,500 square kilometres.
Bidiya Sands is also known as Wahiba Sands, and the easiest entrances are at Bidiyah Castle, reached by gravel road before the sand tracks, and at Al Wasil.

rejectedClaims: A headline population for the wilayat. Figures circulating for Bidiya could not be traced to a census table, so none appears and the page argues from terrain instead.

Any individual dune height. Only the over 100 metres description is published, so the twelve heights inside the project are teaching values and are labelled as such in the project, the pitfalls note and the FAQ.
A road distance to anywhere other than Muscat. The 230 kilometre figure is the only one traced to a source, and it is itself rounded.
